## Summary

**PMUL** (Vector multiply): Vector multiply short.

## Details

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Operation | `a x b → d` |
| Syntax | `PMULH <vea>,b,d`<br>`PMULL <vea>,b,d`<br>`PMUL88 <vea>,b,d` |
| Short | Vector multiply short |
| Description | Pmul\_ is 4 word vector signed multiply. Pmulh keeps upper 16 bits (31..16). Pmull keeps lower 16 bits (15..0). Pmul88 keeps the middle part (23..8). |
| Condition codes | not affected |

### Encoding

| Word | Bits | Content |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | 15–9 | `1111111` |
| 1 | 8 | A |
| 1 | 7 | B |
| 1 | 6 | D |
| 1 | 5–3 | Mode |
| 1 | 2–0 | Register |
| 2 | 15–12 | b |
| 2 | 11–8 | d |
| 2 | 7–2 | `000110` |
| 2 | 1–0 | T |

- T type
- 0=pmul88
- 1=pmula (next page in the original)
- 2=pmulh
- 3=pmull

### Example

```asm
    pmulh    d0,d1,d2
```

```text
vea d0: 00 02 00 20 02 00 FF FF
b d1: 12 34 12 34 12 34 12 34
Result:
d d2: 00 00 00 02 00 24 FF FF
Result of pmull d0,d1,d2:
24 68 46 80 68 00 ED CC
Result of pmul88 d0,d1,d2:
00 24 02 46 24 68 FF ED
```

## Differences from AmigaOS / AROS / 68060

- The 68000–68060 have no PMUL. It is new on the 68080.

## Do / Don't

- No rules beyond the details above.
